text: In World War Two, one Polish army unit had a soldier who wrestled his friends, saluted his officers, and was covered in fur. He was a bear.
1942, near Hamadan in Iran. Polish soldiers on the march meet a local boy with an orphaned cub. A Syrian brown bear.
Accounts differ, but the best-known version says the soldiers traded chocolate, canned beef and a pocketknife for him. Deal.
They name him Wojtek, and feed him condensed milk from an old vodka bottle.
He grows. And grows. He learns to wrestle the soldiers, and to salute.
And the soldiers told some wild stories about him. They said he loved a bottle of beer...
...and that he loved the camp showers so much, he used up all the water and got banned from showering alone.
1944. The unit has to ship out to Italy. But animals aren't allowed to travel with the troops.
The solution? They officially register him as a soldier, so he can travel with the unit. Private Wojtek.
At the Battle of Monte Cassino, according to his fellow soldiers, Wojtek helped carry heavy crates of artillery shells, and never dropped one.
The unit was so proud, they made their badge a bear carrying a shell. And Wojtek was promoted to corporal.
After the war, he retired to Edinburgh Zoo in Scotland, where he lived until 1963.
Today there are statues of him across Europe. Corporal Wojtek. The bear who went to war.
